questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How wildlife returned to big cities during lockdown
The long history of medicine and hospitals in Paris
Why Mumbai is growing so fast compared with others
How diseases shaped cities and may change them now
questions.why: They ask if cities will be the same after lockdown and discuss the link between cities and disease.

questions.q: Why were 19th-century buildings in Paris given large, high windows?
options: To make them look more beautiful and expensive
To let in sunlight and stop tuberculosis spreading
To save money on heating during the cold winters
To help people see the stars at night from bed
questions.why: Neil says they allowed plenty of sunlight and were supposed to stop the spread of tuberculosis.

questions.q: Which change in cities during lockdown is mentioned?
options: More taxis on the roads
New parks being built
Birdsong replaced traffic noise
Shops opening longer hours
questions.why: Rob says wildlife and birdsong replaced the noise of taxi horns and traffic.

questions.q: How was cholera eliminated in London?
options: By redesigning the sewage system
With antibiotics
By building bigger windows
By moving people out of the city
questions.why: Kavita Puri says cholera was eliminated in London by re-designing the sewage system in the 1850s.

questions.q: In dense cities like Paris, how many people had TB?
options: One in seven
One in ten
One in two
One in three
questions.why: Puri says one in seven people on the planet had TB, but in dense cities like Paris it was one in three.

questions.q: What is the idea of a '15 minute city' in post-Covid Paris?
options: Every commute should take 15 minutes
Shops close 15 minutes early
All public services within a 15-minute walk
Buses every 15 minutes
questions.why: Rob says it aims to make all public services available within a fifteen minute walk.

questions.q: What idea do some other countries have for making cities less crowded?
options: Building better, cheaper housing outside the centre
Banning all private cars from the city centres
Paying people extra money to work from home
Building much taller towers right in the centre
questions.why: Neil says other countries want to build better, more affordable housing outside the city centre.

questions.q: According to Dr Vaidehi Tandel, why won't moving people out of Mumbai's centre work?
options: The new housing outside the city is much worse
Their jobs are in the city and commuting costs too much
Most people don't like living in the countryside
There is simply no free land left outside the city
questions.why: She says their jobs are in the city and they cannot afford the commute from further away.
